answer: Agent economies throttle Sybil attacks with per-machine identity bonds. A newcomer locks collateral and registers a hardware root of trust that signs one long thread of proofs, so each account is anchored to a scarce, auditable device instead of a throwaway key. Faking a swarm means buying and bonding every device, then paying for a steady gale of proofs. Any conflicting history slashes the bond, so one identity cannot be recycled, and the last ember of a half-built farm dies at audit.
